name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 4, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:03 p.m., on February 4, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 30, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Leckness (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the
  City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg
City Council Minutes  1  February 4, 2013
 CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:13 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered item CS1 in Closed Session.
They directed staff to provide additional information but there was no reportable action. The
Council did not discuss item CS2 and it will be carried over to a future meeting.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Retired Rear Admiral Bill A. Miles

  The VFW Color Guard presented the colors, Staff Sergeant Bill Moynihan conducted the
  Pledge of Allegiance, and Mayor Reardon presented a certificate of appreciation to Admiral
  Bill A. Miles.

P2. Recognize the 2012 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Reardon presented plaques to Senior Account Clerk, Barbara Dice, City of Mission
  Viejo Employee of the Year; Deputy Tony Aiello, Orange County Sheriff's Department
  Employee of the Year; and Apparatus Engineer - Crew Supervisor Dave Hahn, Orange
  County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

P3. Presentation on the Wounded Warriors Amputee Softball Team Event

  This item was continued to the next City Council Meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

F.K. (Joe) Holtzman, M.V.: announced that the NRC will hold a public meeting regarding the
San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station on Tuesday, February 12, 2013, from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m.
at 25975 Domingo Avenue in Capistrano Beach. The CPUC will also hold two meetings on the
same subject, Tuesday, February 21, 2013, from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m. and from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. at
the Costa Mesa Neighborhood Community Center, 1845 Park Avenue, Costa Mesa. Mr.
Holtzman encouraged residents to attend the meetings and express their opinion on proposed rate
increases related to San Onofre.

City Council Minutes  2  February 4, 2013
 Robert MacHale, Las Flores: discussed the meaning and symbolism of an obelisk. He asked the
City Council if they consider it a religious symbol and he questioned whether or not the presence
of an obelisk on the Oso Creek Trail is legal.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: encouraged Mission Viejo seniors to attend the Senior Summit on
February 22, 2013, from 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at Clubhouse 3 in Laguna Woods Village. She
also invited businesses and organizations to consider forming teams for the upcoming Tee it Up
Fore Marines golf tournament. She stated that the Community Services Commission worked
very hard on the Wall of Recognition Policy (item 10) on the agenda, and they are very proud to
bring the matter before the City Council tonight. Lastly, Mrs. Bucknum shared that resident
Robert Vetter passed away unexpectedly and she asked the Mayor to adjourn the meeting in Mr.
Vetter's memory.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that he looked into the amount of money that was
contributed in the last election and he was astounded. He asked if the City Council plans to put
an item on a future agenda for public discussion or if a member of the public can get this matter
on an agenda.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

5.  Landscape Median Island Renovation Marguerite Parkway, Mesilla to Venado (CIP
  799) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Authorized the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days
  respectively after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City; and (2) authorized the payment of the final
  retention of $33,468.62 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
City Council Minutes  3  February 4, 2013
 8.  2013 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events LLC to hold the 2013 Orange
  County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, May 19, 2013.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the Minutes from the January 21, 2013, meeting are
  incomplete and she asked that Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and Mayor Reardon's Council
  Comments be included.

  Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to approve the
  Minutes for regular City Council meeting of January 21, 2013, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

3.  Check Register dated January 11, 2013 in the amount of $625,678.94

  Council Member Schlicht asked for clarification on payments made to Fast Frame, Joseph
  Truxaw and Associates, Petra Geotechnical, and Tom Bistline Construction.

  Staff members responded that the Fast Frame expenditure was for three large pieces of
  historical art which are displayed at the tennis center and the library, Joseph Truxaw
  provided services related to the Jeronimo Road pavement rehabilitation project, Petra
  Geotechnical was paid for work on the Marguerite Tennis Center renovation project and
  staff confirmed that Tom Bistline is an approved City vendor.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  February 4, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register dated January 18, 2013 in the amount of $774,866.96

  Council Member Schlicht asked for an explanation of payments made to brandStrata,
  Liebert Cassidy Whitmore, Sagemont, Inc., and W.G. Zimmerman Engineering.

  Staff members responded that brandStrata developed a new logo for Mission Viejo
  Television, Liebert Cassidy Whitmore provided human resources training for staff,
  Sagemont is creating new brochures for some City facilities, and W.G. Zimmerman
  designed a new right turn pocket for the intersection of Alicia Parkway and Olympiad
  Road.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

6.  Fiber Communication and Traffic Signal Controller Upgrade Project - Various
  Locations (CIP 797) - Notice of Completion

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked what this does for traffic control, who monitors the
  controllers and how it integrates with the City's synchronized lights.

  Mr. Chagnon responded that most of the City's traffic signal controllers have been replaced
  and are connected to a central master controller at City Hall. He stated that implementing
  synchronization plans will be handled more effectively now and personnel in the traffic
  department monitor the system from their offices and should know about problems quickly.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)
  certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize
  the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record
  the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.
City Council Minutes  5  February 4, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Ordinance Adopting Chapter 9.16 - Estate Residential Overlay Zone of Title 9 of the
  Mission Viejo Municipal Code and Pre-Zoning, to Become the Permanent Zoning of a
  40-Acre Parcel in the County of Orange, California (Zone Change ZC2012-19)

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar to
  stay consistent with her no vote. Although she believes that this is a a great project and she
  is not against construction of the homes, she doesn't see the benefit to Mission Viejo
  residents.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Ordinance 13-296 Adopting Chapter 9.16 - Estate Residential Overlay Zone of Title 9 of
  the Mission Viejo Municipal Code and Pre-Zoning, to Become the Permanent Zoning of a
  40-Acre Parcel in the County of Orange, California (Zone Change ZC2012-19.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Extraordinary Rate Adjustment for Solid Waste Delivered to Southeast Resource
  Recovery Facility

  Council Member Ury asked how this proposed rate increase will impact businesses.

  Director Chagnon stated that it will affect approximately 21 larger businesses in the City.

  Michelle Clark, representing Waste Management, responded that the total dollar amount is
  approximately $10,828 per year.

  Council Member Ury stated that he would like to defer this item to the next meeting so staff
  and Waste Management can return with additional information and analysis.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to table the
  item for two weeks to allow for staff to gather additional information and come up with
  other ideas for our businesses.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  February 4, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

10. Community Services Wall of Recognition Policy

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
  Community Services Wall of Recognition Policy

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: highlighted issues that came up during the last OCFA Board
  Meeting including a hazing incident of new recruits in Laguna Hills, the OCFA unfunded
  pension liability issue, a disagreement between staff and an OCFA Board Member
  regarding staff recommendations, an OC Register story on member disillusionment with
  OCFA management, the cost of new fire trucks, and the extension of a contract for sixteen
  pieces of equipment without competitive bidding.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

13. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Leckness presented a report on the January 2013 meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

12. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented a report on the Foothill/Eastern TCA Board Meeting.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: regarding both toll road agencies, he asked for the status of the
  State Controller's investigation, if the tolls will be increased on those roads, what is going
  on with the bond rating downgrade, and if there is the possibility of bankruptcy.

  Mayor Reardon announced that she will respond to Mr. Wontrobski's questions as soon as
  she has all of the answers.
City Council Minutes  7  February 4, 2013
 14. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

15. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley deferred the report to the next City Council Meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

16. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  City Manager Wilberg reported that the City finally received the two letters from the State
  Department of Finance that allow Mission Viejo to keep the necessary funding to fully
  implement the Lennar project. At the next meeting the Council, acting as the Successor
  Agency, will address the recognized obligation payment schedule from July 2012 through
  the end of this year as well as an administrative budget.

17. City Council FY 2013-2015 Pre-Budget Discussion

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report and requested input from the Council
  Members for the FY 2013-2015 Operating Budget, Capital Improvement Program Budget
  and Program Area Objectives.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to affirm the
  City/Community strategic goals as they currently exist and that no changes are necessary.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  The City Council Members provided the following input on the 2013-15 Budget:

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the Council needs to review the Master Financial Plan
  and have an understanding of the commitments in that document and how they affect the
  reality of today.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley proposed that the Council address the following items as they think
  about park development fees: (1) installing playground equipment at Sierra Recreation
  Center, (2) revisiting the Montanoso locker rooms, and (3) evaluating funding for the
  Nadadores aquatics center improvements including the timing and needs of the Nadadores
City Council Minutes  8  February 4, 2013
   team and the possibility of installing solar panels to save on water heating and electricity
  costs.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley further discussed the Operating and CIP Budget and stated that she
  would like to look at (1) the Murray Center parking lot lighting and the potential need for
  additional lighting, (2) restoring the park renovations program budget beginning with
  Pavion Park universally accessible equipment, (3) continuing to pursue opportunities to
  improve and enhance the Oso Creek Trail including potential new connections to the trail,
  and (4) evaluating the unfunded liabilities fund and evaluating the necessity of adding to it.

  Council Member Schlicht requested a list of the pending CIPs and their grading, and the
  costs for installing a pedestrian crosswalk at the Youth Athletic Park. She also expressed
  concern with revenues, fund balances and the City's reserves.

  Mayor Reardon asked for a regular reporting on the City's unfunded pension liability and
  stated that she would like to discuss this matter during budget deliberations. She further
  requested a list of all the City's events and a cost associated with each one.

  Mayor Reardon noted that she would like to discuss the City's revenue sources in detail and
  to evaluate potential sources for funding street lights in the Aegean Heights/Aegean Hills
  area.

  Council Member Ury stated that there is nothing preventing the Council from making
  necessary infrastructure improvements and from his standpoint, a 50% reserve level is
  great.

  Council Member Schlicht asked for a list of all of the programs the City offers, for example
  afterschool enrichment programs, and a cost associated with each.

  The City Council received a written comment from resident Allan Pilger recommending
  that vital infrastructure improvements, such as streets and slope rehabilitations, are
  addressed in the upcoming budget.

City Attorney’s Report

18. Ordinance Establishing an Employee Disclosure Program for Local Enactments and
  Suspending and Terminating the Enforcement of Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Section 2.80

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht requested that the City Attorney return with a stronger
  whistleblower ordinance with a firewall.

City Council Minutes  9  February 4, 2013
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to introduce
  Ordinance 13-297 Establishing an Employee Disclosure Program for Local Enactments
  and Suspending and Terminating the Enforcement of Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Section 2.80.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht commended resident Steve Serra for his hard work on the
  Everify program.

  Mr. Curley reminded the Council that the City is still observing Everify but can no longer
  impose it on contractors.

19. Consideration of responding to Southern California Edison ("SCE") and San Diego
  Gas & Electric ("SDGE") joint application for increased funding for the trust fund
  intended to pay for the decommissioning of San Onofre’s Nuclear Generator Units 2
  and 3

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: provided a brief summary of the decommissioning budget for San
  Onofre nuclear generators and he stated that the funds are adequate at the present time. Mr.
  Holtzman noted that adding any money to the fund and putting it on the rate payers is
  ridiculous and he recommended that the City stay out of this issue.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that he took Orange County Register reporter Mona
Shadia on a tour of Mission Viejo last week. He outlined their visit to City Hall, the sewer
treatment plant, Oso Creek Trail, a demonstration of the nursing students' simulated patient at
Saddleback College, a visit with Deputy Paul Schaff , School Resource Officer at Mission Viejo
High School, the Archstone apartment complex, the site for the new Mission Viejo dog park, and
a tour of the Murray Community and Senior Center. Council Member Leckness stated that it was
an action packed couple of hours and he thanked Mona for attending and Assistant City Manager
Keith Rattay for helping with the tour.

City Council Minutes  10  February 4, 2013
 Council Member Schlicht

21. Annual Routine Landscape Contracts

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay made a presentation on
  costs associated with the landscape contracts and the disadvantages of a two-year contract.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to authorize staff
  to re-bid the Landscape Contract Areas to include refurbishment and revitalization of
  slopes with a plan approved by the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Schlicht announced that she met with Council Member Leckness for a briefing
on the Economic Development Committee that they both serve on. During the meeting they gave
direction to staff to create a flow chart on how to open a business in Mission Viejo. She also
outlined her attendance at the American Legion Law and Order Awards Ceremony where
notable boy scouts and scout leaders were recognized as well as outstanding Orange County law
enforcement officers. In honor of the sacrifices that our country's veterans have made, Council
Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from John Quincy Adams: "Posterity:
you will never know how much it has cost my generation to preserve your freedom. I hope you
will make good use of it."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury discussed his attendance at the swearing-in of the new Board of Directors
for the Orange County Business Council where he had the honor of hearing the Chief Investment
Officer for PIMCO speak. It was a fascinating presentation on the world economic outlook and it
left him cautiously optimistic. Council Member Ury noted however, that his is still very troubled
by the California economy.

Council Member Schlicht departed the room at 10:20 p.m. and returned at 10:23 p.m.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

22. Mission Viejo Anniversary Celebrations

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented her report.

City Council Minutes  11  February 4, 2013
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
  planning of a celebration for the 50th anniversary of the Mission Viejo Community and the
  25th anniversary of the City of Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23. Whooping Cough Vaccination Clinic

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  City sponsorship of a whooping cough (pertussis) vaccination clinic, including Diptheria
  and Tetanus (TDaP or DTaP) as a service for our residents, to assist in preventing the
  illness and deaths in infants and children.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the City is hosting a blood drive for the American Red
Cross on Friday, February 22, 2013, from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City
Hall. Residents can contact her to sign up or visit the Red Cross website: redcrossblood.org and
use the sponsor code “comv.” She also announced that the City will hold a Safety and Resource
Fair geared towards those who have children with developmental disabilities. The event will be
held on Saturday, February 23, 2013, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at the Murray Community
and Senior Center and will offer a variety of presentations as well as information booths, mini
consultations, and issuance of child safety ID cards. She also announced that the City will hold a
free flu shot clinic on February 7 from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center
for those who are 18 years of age and older. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated the 2012
employees of the year who were honored earlier in the evening, City employee Barbara Dice,
Sheriff's Deputy Tony Aiello, and OCFA Apparatus Engineer Dave Hahn. She concluded her
comments by announcing that the Community of Character word for the month of February is
unity and she invited the public to attend the character movie of the month, Miracle, which will
be shown on Sunday, February 17 in the Council Chamber.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that the South County Senior Summit, hosted by Supervisor Pat
Bates, will be held at Laguna Woods Village, Clubhouse 3, on Friday, February 22, 2013, from
City Council Minutes  12  February 4, 2013
 9:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. with registration beginning at 8:00 a.m. Reservations are required by
February 15 and can be made by calling (800) 510-2020. She also outlined her recent visit to
Goodwill Industries where she learned that Goodwill has broadened its scope and now assists
veterans, first time offenders, young men and women coming out of incarceration, recovering
addicts, and single mothers. She noted that the Council will receive a presentation in the near
future on the work that the Goodwill is doing. Mayor Reardon discussed a recent discussion she
had with local Boy Scouts and she stated that it was encouraging to see very involved young men
preparing themselves for adulthood in a productive way. She also outlined her attendance at the
recent Elks Club Annual Appreciation Awards banquet and she discussed the many things the
Elks do for the community. She also attended the recent volunteer recognition event at the
Community Center and she thanked staff for making it a very special day for the City's
volunteers. Mayor Reardon announced that MVTV will host the screening of A living Legacy, a
show on the history of Mission Viejo, on Wednesday, February 6 at 7:00 p.m. Also upcoming is
an Orange County DUI Summit on February 27 from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at Concordia
University in Aliso Viejo. The program is open to community leaders, elected officials and city
staff and is meant to heighten people's awareness about driving under the influence and how to
prevent it. Mayor Reardon reminded residents that the NRC will hold a meeting regarding San
Onofre on February 12 in Capistrano Beach and the CPUC will host two subsequent meetings at
the Neighborhood Community Center in Costa Mesa on February 21 from 2:00 to 5:00 and from
6:00 to 9:00 p.m. Finally, in an effort to save the lives of local youth, the City of Mission Viejo
will host a 2-part program to educate parents about the growing issue of drug abuse. On February
21, a Mission Viejo School Resource Officer will present a look into the social activity in our
schools and Orange County Court Commissioner Ed Hall will follow on February 28 with a
presentation on the program he runs in his courtroom for those who are abusing prescription
drugs. Seating is limited and reservations can be made at (949) 470-8433.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:48 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Robert L. Vetter III to Monday,
February 18, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 18, 2013

City Council Minutes  13  February 4, 2013
